The '''Bajaj Group''' is an Indian multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] founded by [[Jamnalal Bajaj]] in [[Mumbai]] in 1926.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Lalatendu |date=2026-05-11 |title=Bajaj@100: “The next 100 years of Bajaj will be about building ecosystems“ |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/bajaj100-the-next-100-years-of-bajaj-will-be-about-building-ecosystems/article70966532.ece |access-date=2026-06-10 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The group's official website claims to hold 40 companies with a market capitalization of Rs. 14 lakh crores (~US$ 167 billion). Its flagship automotive company, [[Bajaj Auto|Bajaj Auto,]] is among the world's leading producers of two- and three-wheelers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bajaj Auto Summary: Latest Updates and Details |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/bajaj-auto-ltd/summary |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=India Infoline |language=en}}</ref> The group operates across a range of industries, including [[automobiles]], home appliances, heavy electricals, lighting, iron and steel, insurance, travel, and finance, among others.

The group was founded informally by Bachhraj Bajaj, with a [[Ginning|cotton ginning]] factory in [[Wardha]], [[Maharashtra]], in 1905. Following his death in 1906, his adopted grandson—Jamnalal Bajaj, ran the business for two decades and then established it formally as an industrial and trading business in Mumbai in 1926, named Bachhraj Factories.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Das |first=Sohini |date=12 May 2026 |title=100 years on, Bajaj Group begins to build anew for India's future growth |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/100-years-on-bajaj-group-begins-to-build-anew-for-india-s-future-growth-126051101178_1.html |url-status=live |access-date=9 June 2026 |website=Business Standard|last2=Saha|first2=Manojit|last3=Sahu|first3=Ram Prasad}}</ref>

== Leading figures ==

===Kamalnayan Bajaj (1915 – 1972)===

[[Kamalnayan Bajaj]], the elder son of Jamnalal Bajaj, returned to India after completing his education at the [[University of Cambridge]], [[England]], to assist his father in both business and social service. He played a key role in expanding the Bajaj Group by diversifying its operations into the manufacture of scooters, three-wheelers, cement, alloy castings, and electrical equipment. In 1954, He took over the active management of the Bajaj Group companies and led them towards significant growth and success. 

===Ramkrishna Bajaj (1924 – 1994)===
In 1972[[Ramkrishna Bajaj|, Ramkrishna Bajaj]], the younger son of Jamnalal Bajaj, assumed leadership of the Bajaj Group after the death of his elder brother, Kamalnayan Bajaj. Alongside his business responsibilities, he dedicated much of his time and energy to social service and welfare initiatives. Ramkrishna Bajaj strongly believed in youth development and nation-building.

In 1961, he was elected Chairman of the [[World Assembly of Youth|World Assembly for Youth]] (India). He also served as the Managing Trustee of the Indian Youth Centres Trust, which established the Vishwa Yuvak Kendra in 1968 — a prominent youth development organization focused on leadership, education, and community service.

=== Rahul Bajaj (1938 – 2022) ===

[[Rahul Bajaj]], the chairman emeritus and former managing director (until 2005) of the Group, was the grandson of [[Jamnalal Bajaj]]. He completed his schooling at the [[Cathedral and John Connon School]], Mumbai; and then attended the [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi|St Stephen's College]], Delhi; [[Government Law College, Mumbai|Government Law College]], Mumbai; and [[Harvard University]]. He took over control of the Group in 1965 and led it to be one of India's largest conglomerates.<ref>{{Cite news|title=WHO IS RAHUL BAJAJ|work=Business Standard|url=https://www.business-standard.com/about/who-is-rahul-bajaj|access-date=2020-05-27}}</ref> In 2001, he was awarded [[Padma Bhushan]], India's third-highest civilian award.

==Corporate Social Responsibility==
Jamnalal Bajaj was a disciple of [[Mahatma Gandhi]] and had close personal relationship with him. He has been described in the media as Gandhi's fifth adopted son.<ref name=":0" /> The Bajaj Group runs several charitable organizations<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bajaj Group {{!}} Devex |url=https://www.devex.com/organizations/bajaj-group-180481 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=www.devex.com}}</ref>, and is known for its various CSR initiatives, mostly focusing on skilling and education, health, livelihood, water conservation, and other areas.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Das |first=Sohini |last2=Lele |first2=Abhijit |date=22 March 2024 |title=Bajaj group commits Rs 5,000 crore for social impact initiatives in 5 years |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/bajaj-group-commits-rs-5-000-cr-for-social-initiatives-under-bajaj-beyond-124032200719_1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219104243/https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/bajaj-group-commits-rs-5-000-cr-for-social-initiatives-under-bajaj-beyond-124032200719_1.html |archive-date=2026-02-19 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref> In March 2024, the group committed Rs. 5,000 crore to social impact initiatives for the following five years.<ref name=":1" />
